The floor then moves **into the shared primitives** (#559), because every sweep up to and including #542 raised controls one callsite at a time (`min-h-11 md:min-h-0`) while `Button` (`h-8` default / `h-7` sm / `h-9` lg) and `Input` (`h-8`) stayed below the floor by default — so each new screen re-opened the hole and the floor held only where someone remembered to type the class: the three **text** button sizes and `Input` now carry `max-md:min-h-11` in the variant itself, and #542's per-callsite sprinkles are removed as redundant in the same pass. `icon*` is deliberately excluded (square — a bare `min-h-11` renders it 44×32; the mobile-visible icon buttons stay hand-floored to `size-11` per #510/#511/#535, the rest are absolutely-positioned dialog/sheet/sidebar close affordances), `xs`/`icon-xs` stay dense on purpose, and a callsite that genuinely needs a denser control opts out with `max-md:min-h-0` (tailwind-merge lets the callsite win). The same pass closes **Settings**, the surface #542 named but never reached — the verification found ~25 controls between 20px and 36px there, and the reason none of them tripped the gate is that no `settings-mobile.spec.ts` existed and no Settings component had a unit test, so `qa-strict` stayed green on *other* surfaces' coverage. What the primitives cannot reach is hand-floored: the three `SettingsScreen` `<select>`s (at the time there was **no `ui/select.tsx`** — all 34 `<select>` callsites hand-rolled `h-9`, 28 of them dialogs, so a shared select primitive was deferred to #541, which added it), the checkbox/radio hit rows in `SettingsScreen` / `BackupPanel` / `RestorePanel`, and the three Settings text links. The floor's last hidden hole was not a missed callsite but a **wrong engine** (#572): `h-8` / `max-md:min-h-11` on `Input` are only a promise the platform has to keep, and for the temporal input types iOS Safari does not keep it — it draws a **native control that holds its own intrinsic width and height**, so on a real iPhone the Entry screen's `grid-cols-2 items-end` row rendered the `type="date"` field taller than its `type="month"` sibling (bottom-aligning the cells, which visibly dropped the "Month" label out of line) and overflowing its column into the `gap-3`, the two reading as one continuous bar. All 39 `type="date"` / `type="month"` callsites across 30 files go through the primitive, so the reset lands once — `appearance-none`, scoped to the five temporal types (`date` / `month` / `week` / `time` / `datetime-local`, the last three unused today) rather than applied to every input, because on `type="file"` it would strip the platform's Choose-file button that the primitive's `file:*` classes style rather than replace. The outer `appearance` was the whole gap: Tailwind's preflight already normalises the WebKit shadow parts *inside* the control (`::-webkit-date-and-time-value` gets `min-height: 1lh` + `text-align: inherit`, `::-webkit-datetime-edit` an unpadded inline-flex), but preflight touches `appearance` for no input type. This row's own history is the lesson: #541 explicitly measured these fields as fitting "in full at ~157px" and cleared them, in **Chrome DevTools device mode** — which emulates viewport, DPR, touch and UA string but still renders with Blink and Chrome's own form controls, leaving every platform-owned thing (form widgets, native pickers, font fallback, dvh, safe-area) untested — so a mobile finding taken there is not evidence about a phone. Playwright cannot close that gap either: a `webkit` project runs WebKit's *desktop* form controls, not iOS's UIKit-backed ones, so the pixel truth for the temporal types is a real-device check and the suite pins the class contract only. The same real-device pass found two more of the same shape. **`<select>` had the identical native-metrics problem** — the control was the right width but visibly shorter than the text field beside it, because iOS honours a select's width and ignores its height while the platform appearance is intact — which means #541's floor never actually held there either; the reset is the only way the height lands and it takes the platform arrow with it, so **#541's deliberate "keep the native arrow" decision is reversed** and the app draws its own chevron (`--select-chevron` in `index.css`, themed per mode, lucide's `chevron-down` path so it matches the icon set, delivered as a background image because a `<select>` can host neither child markup nor a pseudo-element, with `pr-8` reserving its room). #541's actual *goal* survives the reversal untouched: a native `<select>` still opens iOS's native sheet or wheel on tap regardless of appearance — what the platform draws in the page and what it opens over the page are independent — so only the in-page arrow changed. **Pagination was simply missed by the whole B-series**: `PaginationControls` rendered one link per page unconditionally, so the control's width grew with the data and a long history ran its last pages and the Next arrow off the right edge of a phone, unreachable, while the `PaginationEllipsis` primitive to prevent it sat unused since the control was written. It now renders a window (`lib/pageWindow.ts`) of **constant item count** (`siblings * 2 + 5`, so paging never resizes the control or reflows its neighbours — near the ends the run of numbers extends into the slot the absent ellipsis would have held, and a gap covering exactly one page spells that page out rather than hiding nothing behind an ellipsis that costs the same slot), with first and last always one tap away, and `siblings` chosen by width alone: 0 below 768px where seven floored items is all 390px holds, 1 above. Its tap targets were also below the floor, for the documented reason that `size="icon"` is the one `Button` family #559 skips — so a page number carries `max-md:size-11` in the primitive rather than at the two callsites (Income list, every detail-page history section), the non-interactive ellipsis matches it so a 32px item doesn't read as a misalignment in a 44px row, and prev/next take `max-sm:w-11` — `sm` not `md`, because their labels are `hidden sm:block`, so they are icon-only *below 640px* (where Button's height-only floor left them 44×34) and text buttons above it that a 44px width cap would squash. The same pass then found the floor's premise failing outright on the **row action menus**: the ⋮ on every card was **completely dead on iOS Safari** — not mispositioned, not opening-then-closing, the content never mounted — because Radix's menu trigger opens on `pointerdown` or the Enter/Space/ArrowDown keys and has **no `click` path at all**, and mobile WebKit was not delivering a usable `pointerdown` to that button. The discriminator that identified it: the same phone opens every Create/Edit dialog fine, and Radix's *dialog* trigger opens on `click` — so `click` arrives, `pointerdown` does not, and the four row menus were the only thing in the app depending on the event iOS withholds. `useMenuOpenOnClick` (in `ui/dropdown-menu.tsx`, used by `RowActionsMenu` / `IncomeRowMenu` / `SnapshotRowMenu` / `TransactionRowMenu`) adds the missing path as a **controlled root plus a click handler that opens only when the menu is closed**, so wherever `pointerdown` already worked Radix has set `open` before the click lands and the fallback self-cancels; no `preventDefault`, so Radix's own path and the keyboard affordances are untouched. It also carries `modal: false`, since none of these menus has a claim to modality (no focus trap, no need to freeze the page) while Radix's default `modal` engages react-remove-scroll's body scroll lock plus `pointer-events: none` on `<body>` — free on desktop WebKit, treacherous in mobile WebKit, which ignores `overflow: hidden` on body for touch scrolling. Unlike the platform-metrics rows above, this one is **not** a class-contract stand-in: dispatching a bare `click` with no `pointerdown` is exactly what the phone was doing, so jsdom reproduces the failure and the guard is a real regression test (reverting the hook turns it red). The floor itself then had to reach **what the trigger opens**, which no sweep had touched: `py-1` + `text-sm` is a ~28px row, so the menu that a floored `size-11` trigger exists to reach handed a phone two under-floor targets. `max-md:min-h-11` now sits on every interactive item kind in the primitive (`DropdownMenuItem`, `CheckboxItem`, `RadioItem`, `SubTrigger`); the non-interactive parts (`Label`, `Separator`, `Shortcut`) stay dense on purpose, since they are not targets and padding them only makes the menu taller. Last, **truncated select labels in the narrow dialog shell**: a `grid-cols-2` row inside `DialogContent` (`sm:max-w-sm`, so ~170px per column at *every* width — there is no wider layout to fall back to, which is why these stack unconditionally rather than under a `md:` divergence) leaves ~128px of text after the field's padding and the new chevron's `pr-8`, about 18 characters. Five callsites overran it and now hold a full-width row each: income **category** (`CreateIncomeDialog` + `EditIncomeDialog`, whose date field goes full-width with it, and which must agree since a member picks a category on create and re-reads it on edit), **bond type** (`CreateBondDialog` — `EditBondDialog` already had it full-width, so the two now agree; the **currency** field that shared the row does not follow it to full width but moves beside the **face value** it denominates, at the same `grid-cols-[1fr_120px]` split the income dialog uses for amount+currency, with the **placement date** dropping to its own row below the pair — three characters do not earn a full row. Currency is required for either bond type but only the government-primary branch has a monetary field to sit beside, so it is defined once in the component and placed in both branches, keeping a row to itself in the secondary-market branch, where the position is opened by a later Buy transaction and there is no amount here at all), and the **principal/interest disposition** pair (`Create`/`EditMaturityTransactionDialog`, both children of one row, so the row itself becomes single-column). Full width rather than a tighter split is deliberate: it is the only version that survives a locale with longer wording than EN/ID. The ranking lesson repeats the epic's 390px one — a **static width estimate mis-ranked which fields were actually broken**: arithmetic flagged the time-deposit rollover policy (32 chars) and bond coupon disposition (27) as the worst, but both already sat in full-width rows and read fine on the device, while the three it scored as merely borderline (16–18 chars) were the ones truncating. A 390px pass scoped what actually breached the bar, and most of the suspected breaks did **not**: the forms fit a 390x844 viewport with the footer reachable, and the unconditional two-column rows render a `type="date"` field and its picker icon in full at ~157px — so per the doctrine's "merely cramped stays single-layout" they were left alone rather than stacked. Three things did breach. First, **`<select>` had no primitive to floor**: all 34 callsites hand-rolled `h-9 rounded-md border border-input bg-background px-3 text-sm` at 36px, so unlike `Button`/`Input` after #559 every new form re-opened the hole — `ui/select.tsx` now carries the same `max-md:min-h-11` contract (plus `text-base md:text-sm`, which is load bearing rather than cosmetic: iOS Safari zooms the viewport when a control under 16px takes focus, which the old `text-sm` selects did on every tap), and all 34 callsites are migrated. Second, the **ownership radios** had no hit row: the native ~13px dot sat in a `flex items-center gap-2` label about 20px tall. The `<label>` already wrapped its input so tapping the word worked — what was missing was a target to aim at — and because all 22 position Create/Edit dialogs had hand-inlined the same block it could not be fixed in one place, so it is extracted to a shared `OwnershipField` (both options now in `max-md:min-h-11` rows splitting the full width on phones, natural inline width from 768px). The extraction also collapses ~950 duplicated lines, standardises on `common:` (the `investments:ownership.*` keys were byte-identical duplicates in both locales and are deleted), and scopes the radio-group `name` per dialog — eight of them shared a bare `ownership_type`, which would have let two mounted dialogs steal each other's selection. Third, the one **`grid-cols-3`** row (liability term / start / maturity) leaves ~100px per column at 390px and truncated the year off both date fields, so it alone stacks below 768px. Two non-breaching cleanups ride along: `max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto` moves into `DialogContent` (twelve tall dialogs passed exactly those classes by hand and 31 did not — purely defensive, since nothing observably clipped, but a `fixed` translate-centred shell has no other way to reach a footer once content outgrows the viewport), and the two-column rows get `[&>*]:content-end` so a wrapped label in one column no longer desynchronises the inputs' baselines. | INV-PRESENTATION-06 | The shared Position Create/Edit dialog scaffold (`PositionFormDialog`, ADR-0043 follow-on / #334) owns the plumbing every per-type dialog duplicated: the dialog shell + header, the `<form>` wrapper, the **shared error envelope** (`errorMessage`, the ADR-0027 face), and the footer (cancel + submit with a distinct pending label + disabled-in-flight). It exposes two modes — **create** (self-triggering, owns its own open state, resets via `onClosed` on close) and **edit** (controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange`, no trigger) — and hands the caller a `close` callback through `onSubmit(close)` so the type keeps its own payload mapping and submit guards while the scaffold owns dismissal. The field **body stays hand-written** per type (no field-config DSL); the dirty-guard is deliberately out of scope. Verified in `PositionFormDialog.test.tsx` (synthetic body — asserts the shell contract, not one type's fields) | `frontend/src/components/dialogs/PositionFormDialog.test.tsx` |
| INV-PRESENTATION-09 | The app paints in its **bundled** typeface, not the platform's — the first family the app tree resolves is `"Geist Variable"` (from `@fontsource-variable/geist`, shipped in the bundle), with the system stack demoted to a fallback tail that applies only if the webfont fails. The rule lives in exactly one place (`--font-sans`, reaching the tree through the `html { @apply font-sans }` base layer); a competing `font-family` on `body` or any wrapper above the app silently beats it by inheritance, which is how the app spent its pre-#565 life downloading a woff2 on every cold load and then rendering in `system-ui`. Not a cosmetic row: `system-ui` resolves to a **different physical font per platform**, so while the override held, every text-width assertion in the suite was platform-dependent — the #562 settings carry-over copy measured 268.6px locally and 301px on the Linux CI runner for the same string (~12%), which is what makes width-sensitive copy assertions reproducible now that it's fixed. It is also the screen half of a two-sided contract: the PDF report renderer embeds the same Geist (`backend/internal/reports/pdf/render.go`), so an exported report and the screen it came from are one typeface. E2E-native rather than vitest because jsdom has no font stack and does not resolve `@apply`, so the regression is invisible to a unit test; the check pairs the computed first family with a canvas measurement against the generic fallback, since `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` both when a face is loaded and when no matching `@font-face` exists at all (it reported `true` throughout the bug).
